title: Structural Traps — Cold Starts and Critical Mass

patterns.title: Cold Starts and Critical Mass
patterns.domain: Dependency and feasibility traps, with strategic coordination and feedback

sources.title: Mark Granovetter (1978), Threshold Models of Collective Behavior
sources.supports: Individual behavioral thresholds and how their distribution produces different aggregate outcomes.
sources.boundary: Formal theoretical model, not a measured participation threshold for Nora's invented service. The article does not identify its simultaneous assurance game with every feature of Granovetter's sequential model.

sources.title: Michael L. Katz and Carl Shapiro (1994), Systems Competition and Network Effects
sources.supports: The publisher abstract describes adoption, compatible components, and network effects on value.
sources.boundary: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record read. Author-hosted full-text requests failed; no detailed proposition or empirical estimate from the unread full text is attributed.

sources.title: Andrew Chen (2021), The Cold Start Problem, chapter 6: The Atomic Network
sources.supports: Atomic-network definition; concentrating useful participation in a bounded initial network; contrast between workplace teams and multi-sided payment networks. Read printed pages 71–79.
sources.boundary: Practitioner synthesis and retrospective business cases, not controlled evidence that any prescribed launch strategy causes success. No historical first-credit-card claim, acquisition statistic, or financial recommendation is made.

sources.title: Damon Centola, Joshua Becker, Devon Brackbill, Andrea Baronchelli (2018), Experimental Evidence for Tipping Points in Social Convention
sources.supports: Observed tipping dynamics around a 25% committed minority in an artificial incentivized naming-convention experiment and explicit rejection of a universal 25% threshold.
sources.boundary: Changing an established convention is different from starting an empty service. The study's setting and incentives limit transfer; no minimum viable network size for a real community is inferred.

patterns.short_description: Build enough relevant participation in the same setting for joining and returning to become worthwhile, then check whether the activity persists without temporary support.
use_when: What makes joining worthwhile before the other side arrives?
Nora launches a local secondhand marketplace. Buyers need useful listings; sellers need serious buyers.
goals: Recognize the familiar predicament before specialist terminology.
Explain the defining mechanism and distinguish neighboring concepts.
Participation is allowed but may be unattractive. Needs, location, current supply, and usable demand matter; signups, first trades, continued activity, and profitability are distinct.
Separate hypothetical behavior, model results, documented cases, and practical editorial proposals.
mechanisms: Concentrate current bicycles and relevant buyers in one district; observe completed exchanges and activity after temporary support changes.
Suitable goods, willing buyers, reliable collection, and activity after support ends still need testing.
example_user_queries: What makes joining worthwhile before the other side arrives?

visual.question: What makes joining worthwhile before the other side arrives?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. Few suitable listings discourage buyers; few serious buyers discourage sellers. Nora concentrates available bicycles and relevant buyers within one district, then checks real trades and later activity. Change: Build one usable local buyer–seller network before expanding. Limitation: Suitable goods, willing buyers, reliable collection, and activity after support ends still need testing.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. The upper return path shows the cold-start dependency between useful supply and demand. The lower launch sequence concentrates relevant matching rather than merely increasing signups. Assistance costs resources, and early trades do not establish continued activity or profitability.
